_about: Hand-written key points for pyt-medicine.html (27 Nov 2026, lead). Samples: FMGE recalls, no images.
subject: Medicine
intro: Medicine is the biggest subject in FMGE, and it repeats: ECG changes, electrolytes, endocrine emergencies, the classic signs and the drug of choice. These are the topics that keep coming back, most-asked first, with the one thing to remember about each.

med.card.ecg.note: Heart blocks: first degree PR over 200 ms; Mobitz I PR lengthens then a beat drops; Mobitz II sudden drop (pacemaker); complete block, P and QRS unrelated. Infarct site: II, III, aVF inferior (RCA); V1-V4 anterior (LAD); I, aVL, V5-V6 lateral. Hyperkalaemia: tall tented T, then wide QRS. AF: anticoagulate if CHA2DS2-VASc is 2 or more in men (3 in women).
med.card.ecg.why: A CHA2DS2-VASc score of 3 means a high stroke risk: start oral anticoagulation.

med.card.acs.note: STEMI: primary PCI within 90 minutes, or thrombolysis within 12 hours if PCI is not available. Give aspirin, a P2Y12 blocker, heparin and a statin. Troponin is the marker of choice. Wellens pattern (deep T inversion in V2-V3) warns of critical proximal LAD narrowing.
med.card.acs.why: Deep T inversion in V2-V3 between pains is Wellens syndrome: a critical proximal LAD stenosis.

med.card.hf.note: HFrEF: ACE inhibitor or ARB or ARNI, β-blocker, spironolactone and an SGLT2 inhibitor reduce deaths; diuretics only ease symptoms. BNP or NT-proBNP helps diagnosis. Acute pulmonary oedema: sit up, oxygen, IV furosemide, nitrates.
med.card.hf.why: A β-blocker with an ACE inhibitor is the base of HFrEF treatment; both cut mortality.

med.card.valv.note: Murmurs: aortic stenosis, ejection systolic to the carotids; mitral regurgitation, pansystolic to the axilla; mitral stenosis, mid-diastolic rumble with opening snap. Valsalva and standing make HOCM and mitral valve prolapse louder; almost everything else gets softer. Rheumatic fever is the commonest cause of mitral stenosis in India.
med.card.valv.why: Valsalva reduces venous return, the ventricle gets smaller and the HOCM obstruction gets worse, so the murmur is louder.

med.card.jvp.note: a wave = atrial contraction: absent in AF, large in tricuspid stenosis and pulmonary hypertension, cannon a waves in complete heart block. Large v wave in tricuspid regurgitation. Steep y descent in constrictive pericarditis; Kussmaul sign (JVP rises on breathing in) in constriction.
med.card.jvp.why: In atrial fibrillation the atria do not contract, so the a wave disappears.

med.endo.dm.note: Diagnosis: fasting 126 mg/dL or more, 2-hour 200 or more, HbA1c 6.5% or more. DKA: glucose, ketones, acidosis; treat with fluids first, then insulin infusion, and watch potassium (give it once it is under 5.3). HHS: very high glucose and osmolality without much ketosis. HbA1c shows control over about 3 months.
med.endo.dm.why: HbA1c reflects average glucose over the red cell's lifespan, about 3 months.

med.endo.thy.note: Hyperthyroid: Graves (diffuse goitre, eye signs, TSH-receptor antibodies). Hypothyroid: Hashimoto is the commonest cause where iodine is adequate. TSH is the best screening test. Propylthiouracil in the first trimester, carbimazole otherwise. Thyroid storm: β-blocker, PTU, then iodine an hour later, plus steroids.

med.endo.pit.note: Prolactinoma: the commonest pituitary tumour; cabergoline first. Acromegaly: screen with IGF-1, confirm by failure of GH suppression after a glucose load. Diabetes insipidus: dilute urine; the water deprivation test, then desmopressin separates central from nephrogenic. SIADH: low sodium with concentrated urine.

med.endo.adr.note: Addison: low sodium, high potassium, hypotension, pigmentation; adrenal crisis is treated with IV hydrocortisone and saline. Cushing: the commonest cause is steroid medicine; of the internal causes, a pituitary adenoma (Cushing disease). Screen with the overnight dexamethasone test or 24-hour urine cortisol. Conn: hypertension with low potassium.
med.endo.adr.why: Low BP, low sodium and high potassium after an illness is an adrenal crisis.

med.neph.aki.note: Prerenal: urine sodium under 20, FENa under 1%, bland urine. Acute tubular necrosis: muddy brown granular casts, FENa over 2%. Red cell casts mean glomerulonephritis; white cell casts mean pyelonephritis or interstitial nephritis. Urgent dialysis for refractory potassium, acidosis, fluid overload, uraemic signs.
med.neph.aki.why: Muddy brown granular casts after a long low-BP spell are acute tubular necrosis.

med.neph.ckd.note: Staged by GFR (and albuminuria). Diabetes and hypertension are the commonest causes. Anaemia from low erythropoietin; renal bone disease from high phosphate and low vitamin D (secondary hyperparathyroidism). ACE inhibitors or ARBs slow proteinuric disease.
med.neph.ckd.why: Damaged kidneys make less erythropoietin, so the marrow makes fewer red cells.

med.neph.lyte.note: Hyperkalaemia: first calcium gluconate to protect the heart, then insulin with glucose and salbutamol to shift potassium in, then remove it (binders, dialysis). Hyponatraemia: correct slowly (no more than about 8-10 mmol/L in 24 hours) or osmotic demyelination follows.
med.neph.lyte.why: Calcium gluconate stabilises the heart muscle membrane at once; it does not lower potassium.

med.neph.abg.note: Anion gap = Na − (Cl + HCO3), normal about 12. High-gap acidosis: ketones, lactate, renal failure, methanol, ethylene glycol, salicylates. Normal-gap: diarrhoea, renal tubular acidosis. RTA type 4 (aldosterone lack) has high potassium; types 1 and 2 have low potassium. Winter's formula checks respiratory compensation.
med.neph.abg.why: Type 4 RTA comes from low aldosterone action, so potassium is not excreted.

med.neuro.stroke.note: Anterior cerebral artery: leg weakness more than arm. Middle cerebral: face and arm, aphasia if dominant side. Posterior cerebral: vision loss. Thrombolysis with alteplase within 4.5 hours once a CT has ruled out bleeding. Lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome: PICA or vertebral artery.

med.neuro.cn.note: Trigeminal neuralgia: brief electric pain on touching the face; carbamazepine first. Bell palsy (lower motor neurone facial palsy): steroids within 72 hours; the forehead is weak too, unlike a stroke. Third nerve palsy with a blown pupil = compression (posterior communicating aneurysm).
med.neuro.cn.why: Shock-like facial pain set off by touch is trigeminal neuralgia; carbamazepine is first-line.

med.neuro.move.note: Parkinson: resting tremor, rigidity, slow movement, shuffling gait; loss of dopamine neurons in the substantia nigra. Wilson: low ceruloplasmin, Kayser-Fleischer rings, liver disease. Huntington: CAG repeats, chorea, dementia, autosomal dominant.
med.neuro.move.why: Parkinson disease is a loss of dopamine in the nigrostriatal pathway.

med.neuro.nm.note: Myasthenia: fatigable weakness and ptosis, anti-AChR antibodies, thymoma in some; pyridostigmine. Guillain-Barré: ascending weakness after an infection (Campylobacter), lost reflexes, high CSF protein with normal cells; IVIG or plasma exchange, watch breathing (vital capacity).
med.neuro.nm.why: Weakness that worsens by evening and improves with neostigmine is myasthenia gravis.

med.resp.obs.note: Asthma: reversible obstruction (FEV1 rises 12% and 200 mL after a bronchodilator). COPD: FEV1/FVC under 0.70 after a bronchodilator. In COPD with CO2 retention, aim oxygen saturation at 88-92%. Stopping smoking and long-term oxygen are what improve survival.
med.resp.obs.why: Too much oxygen in COPD can raise CO2; the target saturation is 88-92%.

med.resp.ild.note: Restrictive pattern: FEV1/FVC normal or high, low DLCO. Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: basal crackles, clubbing, honeycombing; pirfenidone or nintedanib slow it. Sarcoidosis: bilateral hilar nodes, non-caseating granulomas, raised ACE and calcium.
med.resp.ild.why: Pirfenidone is an antifibrotic that slows the progression of pulmonary fibrosis.

med.resp.tb.note: India (NTEP): diagnose with sputum CBNAAT/TrueNat, which also shows rifampicin resistance. New case: 2 months HRZE then 4 months HRE, daily, by weight bands. Latent TB treatment for contacts. Treat MDR-TB with the newer all-oral regimens (bedaquiline-based).

med.resp.pl.note: Light's criteria: exudate if pleural/serum protein over 0.5, pleural/serum LDH over 0.6, or pleural LDH over two-thirds of the upper normal serum value. Transudates: heart failure, cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome. In India, a lymphocytic exudate with high ADA suggests TB.
med.resp.pl.why: A pleural to serum protein ratio over 0.5 makes it an exudate.

med.resp.pft.note: Obstructive: FEV1/FVC low, TLC normal or high. Restrictive: FEV1/FVC normal or high, TLC low. DLCO falls in emphysema and fibrosis, and rises in pulmonary haemorrhage and polycythaemia.

med.id.hiv.note: CD4 under 200: Pneumocystis (co-trimoxazole prevention), Kaposi sarcoma. Under 100: toxoplasma, cryptococcus. Under 50: CMV retinitis, MAC. India starts treatment in everyone regardless of CD4 (test and treat), first-line tenofovir, lamivudine and dolutegravir.
med.id.hiv.why: Kaposi sarcoma usually appears when the CD4 count has fallen below 200.

med.id.fever.note: Dengue: thrombocytopenia, rising haematocrit means leakage, NS1 in the first days. Scrub typhus: an eschar; Orientia, spread by mite larvae (chiggers); doxycycline. Leptospirosis: rat urine, jaundice, kidney failure, calf pain. Typhoid: relative bradycardia, blood culture in week 1. Falciparum malaria: artemisinin combinations.
med.id.fever.why: Orientia tsutsugamushi (scrub typhus) is spread by trombiculid mite larvae.

med.id.sepsis.note: Sepsis = infection with organ dysfunction (SOFA up 2 or more). Septic shock: vasopressors needed for MAP 65 or more, and lactate over 2 despite fluids. Give antibiotics within the first hour, 30 mL/kg crystalloid, and noradrenaline as the first vasopressor. Gram-negative endotoxin is lipopolysaccharide.
med.id.sepsis.why: Lipopolysaccharide (endotoxin) in the Gram-negative outer membrane drives the sepsis response.

med.haem.anem.note: Microcytic: iron deficiency (low ferritin, high TIBC) versus thalassaemia trait (normal ferritin, high HbA2). Macrocytic: B12 or folate lack; B12 lack also damages nerves. Haemolysis: high LDH and bilirubin, low haptoglobin, reticulocytes. Plummer-Vinson: iron deficiency, dysphagia from a web, spoon nails.
med.haem.anem.why: Spoon nails, pallor and difficulty swallowing solids in a young woman are Plummer-Vinson syndrome.

med.haem.leuk.note: AML: Auer rods; the M3 type (APML) with t(15;17) causes DIC and responds to all-trans retinoic acid. ALL: the commonest childhood cancer. CML: t(9;22) BCR-ABL, treated with imatinib. CLL: smudge cells in older adults. Hairy cell leukaemia: TRAP positive, dry tap.
med.haem.leuk.why: Needle-shaped inclusions in myeloblasts are Auer rods, which mean AML.

med.haem.coag.note: Haemophilia A (factor VIII) and B (IX): long aPTT, normal PT and platelets, joint bleeds. Von Willebrand: the commonest inherited bleeding disorder. DIC: low platelets and fibrinogen, high D-dimer, long PT and aPTT. TTP: fever, low platelets, haemolysis, kidney and brain signs (ADAMTS13); plasma exchange. Chronic ITP refractory to drugs: splenectomy.
med.haem.coag.why: When chronic ITP does not respond to medicines, removing the spleen gives the best long-term result.

med.rheum.auto.note: Most specific antibodies: anti-dsDNA and anti-Smith (SLE), anti-histone (drug-induced lupus), anti-CCP (rheumatoid arthritis), anti-centromere (limited scleroderma), anti-Scl-70 (diffuse scleroderma), anti-Jo-1 (polymyositis), anti-Ro (Sjögren, neonatal heart block). ANA is the best screening test for SLE.
med.rheum.auto.why: Joint pain, a facial rash and a positive ANA in a young woman point to SLE.

med.rheum.vasc.note: Large vessel: giant cell arteritis (older, headache, jaw pain; start steroids at once to save sight), Takayasu (young women, absent pulses). Medium: Kawasaki (children, coronary aneurysms; IVIG and aspirin), polyarteritis nodosa (hepatitis B). Small: granulomatosis with polyangiitis (c-ANCA), HSP (IgA, palpable purpura in children).
med.rheum.vasc.why: Palpable purpura on the legs, belly pain and joint pain in a child is Henoch-Schönlein purpura (IgA vasculitis).

med.gi.liver.note: Portal hypertension: varices, splenomegaly, ascites. Child with bleeding varices and a big spleen but normal liver function and no ascites: extrahepatic portal vein obstruction. Variceal bleed: terlipressin or octreotide, antibiotics, endoscopic band ligation. Hepatic encephalopathy: lactulose and rifaximin. SAAG of 1.1 or more = portal hypertension ascites.
med.gi.liver.why: Bleeding with splenomegaly but no ascites in a child, with a healthy liver, is extrahepatic portal vein obstruction.

med.gi.hep.note: HBsAg = current infection. Anti-HBs alone = vaccinated. Anti-HBs with anti-HBc IgG = past infection, immune. IgM anti-HBc = acute infection (and the window period). HBeAg = high infectivity. Hepatitis C is now cured with direct-acting antivirals (sofosbuvir-based).
med.gi.hep.why: Anti-HBs without anti-HBc means immunity from the vaccine, not from infection.

med.gi.ibd.note: Crohn: mouth to anus, skip lesions, transmural, fistulas, granulomas, cobblestone mucosa, smoking makes it worse. Ulcerative colitis: rectum upwards, continuous, mucosal only, bloody diarrhoea, pseudopolyps, linked to primary sclerosing cholangitis and toxic megacolon; smoking seems protective.
med.gi.ibd.why: Skip lesions (patches of normal bowel between diseased ones) belong to Crohn's disease.

med.icu.shock.note: Types: hypovolaemic, cardiogenic, distributive (septic, anaphylactic, neurogenic), obstructive (tamponade, tension pneumothorax, massive PE). Anaphylaxis is a type I (IgE) reaction: IM adrenaline 0.5 mg in the thigh first. Neurogenic shock: low BP with a slow pulse.
med.icu.shock.why: A rash and breathing difficulty soon after food is anaphylaxis, a type I (IgE-mediated) reaction.

med.icu.vent.note: ARDS (Berlin): within 1 week, bilateral infiltrates, not explained by heart failure, PaO2/FiO2 300 or less (mild), 200 or less (moderate), 100 or less (severe). Ventilate with low tidal volumes (6 mL/kg ideal weight), PEEP, and prone positioning when severe.
med.icu.vent.why: Bilateral infiltrates with severe hypoxaemia and a normal wedge pressure (not cardiac) is ARDS.

med.icu.score.note: qSOFA (one point each): breathing rate 22 or more, systolic BP 100 or less, altered mentation (GCS under 15). Two or more suggests a high risk of death from sepsis. Lactate is not part of qSOFA.
med.icu.score.why: qSOFA uses only bedside signs; serum lactate is not one of them.

med.tox.op.note: Organophosphates: pinpoint pupils, sweating, secretions, slow pulse, fasciculations. Atropine titrated to dry chest secretions, plus pralidoxime early. Watch for the intermediate syndrome (neck and breathing muscle weakness) after 1-4 days.

med.tox.alc.note: Methanol: blurred or lost vision, high anion gap acidosis. Ethylene glycol: kidney failure with calcium oxalate crystals. Both are treated with fomepizole (or ethanol) and haemodialysis.

med.tox.pcm.note: Toxic dose about 150 mg/kg. N-acetylcysteine refills glutathione and works best within 8 hours, guided by the Rumack-Matthew nomogram from 4 hours. Liver failure peaks at 3-4 days; fulminant failure that meets the King's College criteria needs a liver transplant.

med.tox.snake.note: Viper bites (Russell's viper, saw-scaled viper): local swelling and bleeding, the 20-minute whole blood clotting test is abnormal, kidney failure. Elapids (cobra, krait): paralysis, ptosis, breathing failure; krait bites are painless and at night. Polyvalent anti-snake venom; neostigmine with atropine for cobra paralysis.

med.gen.ct.note: Marfan: fibrillin-1, tall with long limbs, upward lens dislocation, aortic root dilatation and dissection. Homocystinuria: downward lens dislocation and clots. Ehlers-Danlos: collagen defects, stretchy skin, loose joints.
med.gen.ct.why: Marfan syndrome is caused by mutations in the fibrillin-1 gene (FBN1).

med.gen.men.note: MEN1 (menin): parathyroid, pituitary, pancreas. MEN2A (RET): medullary thyroid cancer, phaeochromocytoma, parathyroid. MEN2B (RET): medullary thyroid cancer, phaeochromocytoma, mucosal neuromas, marfanoid build.
med.gen.men.why: Medullary thyroid cancer, phaeochromocytoma and mucosal neuromas are MEN2B, caused by RET mutations.

med.gen.nf.note: NF1 (chromosome 17): café-au-lait spots, axillary freckles, neurofibromas, Lisch nodules (iris hamartomas), optic glioma. NF2 (chromosome 22): bilateral vestibular schwannomas. Both autosomal dominant.
med.gen.nf.why: Lisch nodules, small iris hamartomas, are a feature of neurofibromatosis type 1.

med.nut.vit.note: B1 (thiamine): beriberi, Wernicke (confusion, eye signs, unsteady gait; give thiamine before glucose). B3 (niacin): pellagra, the 3 Ds. B12: megaloblastic anaemia with nerve damage. Vitamin C: scurvy, bleeding gums. Vitamin A: night blindness, Bitot spots. Vitamin D: rickets and osteomalacia.

med.occ.title: Occupational lung disease: silicosis, asbestosis, berylliosis
med.occ.note: Silicosis: upper zones, eggshell calcification of hilar nodes, raises TB risk. Asbestosis: lower zones, pleural plaques; mesothelioma (and lung cancer, worse with smoking). Berylliosis looks like sarcoidosis. Coal workers: Caplan syndrome with rheumatoid arthritis.
med.occ.why: Long asbestos exposure is the classic cause of malignant mesothelioma.
